html:
Massawa is a port on islands off the Red Sea coast of Eritrea, taken by the Ottoman Turks in 1557 and for three centuries the main outlet of the northern Ethiopian highlands.

The Ottomans made it the base of their province of Habesh, cutting the Ethiopian Christian kingdom off from the sea. Egypt took it over in the 19th century, and in 1885 Italy landed there, the first step toward Italian Eritrea, whose capital it was until 1897.

Its coral stone houses and mosques show Ottoman, Egyptian and Italian rule. The town was heavily bombed in the war of independence, when its capture by rebels in 1990 cut off the Ethiopian army. It succeeded old Adulis as Eritrea's gate to the sea.
sum: Massawa is a port on islands off the Red Sea coast of Eritrea, taken by the Ottoman Turks in 1557 and for three centuries the main outlet of the northern Ethiopian highlands.
